demonstrated: AuroraPIC reproduces the tested Maiorov published homogeneous argon Monte Carlo results within the prospectively declared tolerance
that reproduction is robust to a factor-two timestep refinement and a second random seed under the declared gates
the common AuroraPIC transport kernel distinguishes a collision package that disagrees systematically with historical mobility from one that is consistent at all five selected fields
the Phelps-based package passes stationarity, precision, energy-coverage, and historical experimental comparison gates at all five selected fields
two additional fully matched independent particle histories pass every per-run, cross-seed, and ensemble gate
the unchanged Phelps-based package passes a modern ETHZ pressure-resolved pulsed-Townsend mobility comparison at 10, 20, and 30 Td under uncertainty-aware gates
the modern comparison uses an explicitly temporal swarm coefficient that is compatible with AuroraPIC flux drift in this non-ionizing range
not_demonstrated: blind predictive validation because Phelps-based cross sections may use swarm constraints
metrology-grade validation with pointwise experimental uncertainties and pointwise temperature metadata in the distributed table
publication-grade estimation of the full sampling distribution beyond the two matched independent replicas
validation of self-consistent PIC fields, ion transport, boundaries, imported geometry, plasma chemistry, collective behavior, or device observables
assessment: AuroraPIC has reached an independently replicated homogeneous electron-argon transport credibility milestone and now passes a modern, pressure-resolved experimental comparison from 10 to 30 Td. The evidence supports the numerical collision/transport kernel, demonstrates physically meaningful sensitivity to collision data, and spans both modern low-field and historical higher-field measurements. It does not yet justify a general real-case or device-level validation claim.
next_gate: Connect the qualified collision package to a self-consistent canonical PIC benchmark, then qualify boundary/geometry observables before a real-device claim.
